In the run-up to the [[2024 Indian general election]], various media houses and polling agencies carried out [[opinion poll]]s to gauge voting intentions. Results of such polls are displayed in this list.

[[File:Wahlkreise in Indien.svg|350px|thumb|Seats by constituency. As this is a [[First-past-the-post voting|FPTP]] election, seat totals are not determined proportional to each party's total vote share, but instead by the plurality in each constituency]]

== Exit polls ==
The Election Commission of India banned the publication of all [[exit poll]]s starting 48 hours before Phase 1 of the election until the end of Phase 7. This was intended to prevent exit polls from earlier phases affecting voter decisions in later phases. The ban ended after the close of Phase 7 voting at 18:30 IST on 1 June 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-03-29 |title=No exit poll from 7 am on April 19 to 6.30 pm on June 1: EC |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/elections/lok-sabha/india/no-exit-poll-from-7-am-of-apr-19-to-6-30-pm-of-june-1-ec/articleshow/108883088.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-06-01 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

==Reception==
Media outlets known for their [[Politico-media complex|sycophanchy]] [[Godi media|of the BJP]] were accused of exaggerating the scale of BJP's victory in their exit polls in an [[Psychological warfare|attempt to demoralise]] the Opposition campaign.<ref name="d875">{{cite web | title=From India Today to India TV, Zee goes all guns blazing against top media owners | website=Newslaundry | date=2024-06-05 | url=https://www.newslaundry.com/2024/06/05/from-india-today-to-india-tv-zee-goes-all-guns-blazing-against-top-media-owners | access-date=2024-08-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1GePGZljoag |title='Media has made circus of exit polls. Need transparency, more data' — C-Voter founder Yashwant Deshmukh |date=2024-06-16 |last=[[The Print]] |access-date=2026-03-14 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=<!-- Staff writer(s); no by-line --> |date=2024-06-07 |title=How India’s exit polls got the 2024 Lok Sabha election horribly wrong |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/news/exit-polls-were-wrong-lok-sabha-election-2024-bjp-narendra-modi-amit-shah-coalition-bjp-led-alliance-rahul-gandhi/article68262575.ece |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=Frontline |language=en}}</ref> Talking in a show of [[BBC]] Hindi, political strategist [[Yogendra Yadav]] described it as [[crowd manipulation]] orchestrated [[Media manipulation|by the media]] and stated that had these media outlets been honest about the situation on ground, the BJP wouldn't have won even 200 seats (read [[Tinkerbell effect]]).<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=TWV3jH7kc_w5Sght&v=5I22HEPZ8Ow&feature=youtu.be |title=Exit Poll का फटा ढोल और डंकापति का बिखरा शीराज़ा {{!}} NL Tippani 191 |date=2024-06-11 |last=[[newslaundry]] |access-date=2024-10-28 |via=YouTube}}</ref>
